investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-06T10:33–10:41Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never started, so the eval contract was violated at the infrastructure layer before any application code could run.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no node can accept a new peer-pod VM. Preemption was also ruled out ("No preemption victims found"). Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) could not return any evidence, causing a total contract gap for all four required fields. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod stuck unscheduled for 130s.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was captured, consistent with the pod never starting.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing, confirming the probe returned before any agent lifecycle data could be written.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler error, pod stuck 142s, zero evidence keys — same root cause reproduced on a second independent probe run.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error, pod stuck 145s, zero evidence keys — same root cause reproduced on a third independent probe run.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; this call never completes when the pod cannot be scheduled, so no evidence is written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod is unschedulable.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. Supported directly by the scheduler message in failed-check.message and both sibling check messages.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, artificially constraining the schedulable pool to those 2 already-full nodes. This is a contributing structural factor even if capacity were partially restored.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total number of kata.peerpods.io/vm slots across the 2 eligible nodes may be insufficient for concurrent eval probe runs plus any live workloads, causing transient exhaustion under normal load.

Out-of-scope hypothesis — eval runner or contract misconfiguration: the runner branch at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1880-1885 and the contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 254-259 are structurally correct; the failure occurs before the runner can write any evidence, so a code bug in the runner is not supported by the current evidence.

Review the cluster's total kata.peerpods.io/vm slot count against expected concurrent remote agent demand and consider provisioning additional capacity or nodes if the current pool is structurally undersized.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms the failure is not isolated to one probe and that all three checks share the same scheduler-level root cause.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity available on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the failure, the exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and a different scheduling or admission error would need to be investigated.
If a re-run of the probe immediately after the failure succeeded and returned vmIdPresent=true with a valid remoteState, the failure would be transient rather than a sustained capacity exhaustion.

If the pod spec for a remote agent pod did not request kata.peerpods.io/vm as a resource, the scheduler message would indicate a different root cause (e.g., a node label mismatch unrelated to peer-pod capacity).
If only remote-agent-create failed while remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime passed, the failure would be isolated to the create probe rather than a shared infrastructure constraint.

If the 4 non-matching nodes were shown to carry kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity but were excluded by a misconfigured node selector, the primary cause would shift from capacity exhaustion to affinity misconfiguration.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated capacity on each node before attempting remote agent creation, surfacing capacity exhaustion as a distinct pre-condition failure rather than a scheduling timeout.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote agent pod's node selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., >= 3), catching pool shrinkage before it causes scheduling failures.
Add a peer-pod VM slot headroom eval that alerts when available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots across all eligible nodes fall below a configurable minimum, enabling proactive capacity management.

Consider adding a retry-with-backoff eval variant for remote-agent-create that distinguishes transient scheduling delays from sustained exhaustion, reducing false positives from momentary capacity spikes.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-06T10:36–10:41Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the 6-node cluster has zero schedulable nodes for kata peer-pod VMs — 2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no remote agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource, and the remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every attempt to schedule a remote-agent pod times out (~130–148 s per attempt), preventing agent creation and making all downstream state and runtime checks unreachable. This is an infrastructure capacity or configuration constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; the impact is scoped to this observability eval.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. Preemption found no victims, confirming no lower-priority pods are present to evict.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, reducing the schedulable pool to only the 2 kata-capable nodes. If those rules recently changed or node labels drifted, the effective capacity could have dropped without a quota change.

TERTIARY — Cluster under-provisioning: the 6-node cluster may not have enough kata-capable nodes to handle concurrent eval runs plus production workloads simultaneously, causing transient exhaustion during peak scheduling.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — Eval runner scheduling timeout too short: the pod was stuck for 130–148 s across all three checks; if the cluster would eventually schedule the pod after a longer wait, a timeout increase could mask the symptom but would not fix the capacity root cause.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Swarm Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in sequence on 2026-07-06 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting zero available nodes: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner never received any response, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) empty and causing the expected-output contract to fail completely. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agent VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod submitted by the eval runner remained Unschedulable for the full timeout window (~130–149 s), preventing agent creation and all downstream lifecycle and runtime checks from executing. The contract violation (all 5 required evidence fields missing) is a direct consequence of the pod never starting, not a code or configuration defect in the eval runner itself.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: those nodes are structurally ineligible (wrong labels, taints, or zone) for remote-agent pods, reducing the effective scheduling pool to only 2 nodes, both of which are already at capacity.

The eval runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1916) to track and release resources, but if a previous run crashed before cleanup, slots could remain occupied.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-06T10:33–10:41Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never started, so the eval contract was violated at the infrastructure layer before any application code could run.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no node can accept a new peer-pod VM. Preemption was also ruled out ("No preemption victims found"). Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) could not return any evidence, causing a total contract gap for all four required fields. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error, pod stuck 145s, zero evidence keys — same root cause reproduced on a third independent probe run.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod is unschedulable.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. Supported directly by the scheduler message in failed-check.message and both sibling check messages.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, artificially constraining the schedulable pool to those 2 already-full nodes. This is a contributing structural factor even if capacity were partially restored.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total number of kata.peerpods.io/vm slots across the 2 eligible nodes may be insufficient for concurrent eval probe runs plus any live workloads, causing transient exhaustion under normal load.

Out-of-scope hypothesis — eval runner or contract misconfiguration: the runner branch at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1880-1885 and the contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 254-259 are structurally correct; the failure occurs before the runner can write any evidence, so a code bug in the runner is not supported by the current evidence.

The eval runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1916) to track and release resources, but if a previous run crashed before cleanup, slots could remain occupied.

Lower probability — a cluster-level quota or LimitRange on kata.peerpods.io/vm was recently tightened, reducing the number of concurrent VMs the namespace is permitted to schedule. No quota-change evidence is present in the supplied packet.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity available and not exhausted at the time of the eval run, the scheduling-exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different cause (e.g., misconfigured node affinity labels, API-level agent creation error before pod submission) would need to be investigated.
If the remote-agent-create check passed in a concurrent or immediately subsequent run without any cluster changes, it would suggest a transient scheduling race rather than sustained exhaustion.

If the eval runner logs showed the pod was successfully scheduled but the agent process crashed or returned an unexpected response, the root cause would shift from infrastructure capacity to agent runtime behavior.

If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed, it would indicate the failure is isolated to the runtime probe logic rather than shared VM scheduling capacity.

If a node affinity misconfiguration (wrong label key or value on the pod spec) were found in the runner source, it would explain why 4 nodes never match regardless of capacity, making affinity misconfiguration the primary cause rather than resource exhaustion.

Add an orphaned-pod detection eval that lists remote-agent pods older than a configurable threshold (e.g., 10 minutes) and alerts if any are found in Pending or Running state without an active eval session, catching slot leaks before they exhaust capacity.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies at least N nodes in the cluster carry the required labels and taints for remote-agent scheduling, alerting if the eligible node count drops below the minimum needed for concurrent eval runs.

Introduce a historical baseline for the remote-agents eval checks so that verifierContext.history.previousRunCount > 0 and currentlyRegressedFromPass can be evaluated on future failures, enabling regression detection rather than only point-in-time failure reporting.
